points.caption: A useful AI prompt starts with a clear job, trusted context, and a review step.

AI can help a small business draft a service page, answer customer questions, organize research
The quality of the result depends on more than the tool.
It depends on whether the request gives the tool enough direction to make a useful decision.
“Write about websites” leaves too many decisions open.
“Draft the opening section for a service page that helps a homeowner decide whether to request a website consultation” gives the tool a job and a reader.
Ask for a page outline, a customer reply, a list of options, a rewrite, or a review.
Use plain language and explain the next step without promising a ranking or a guaranteed number of leads.
It gives the tool a voice, a customer, and a boundary.
A prompt should identify who will use or read the result.
“Write for a busy owner who understands their service but is not comfortable with marketing software” is more useful than “make it simple.
” If the result will be used in more than one channel, name each audience.
The prompt should not ask one paragraph to do both jobs.
Describe how the answer should sound and what it must avoid.
no unsupported statistics, no jargon, and no claims that require a source.
and speak to the reader as a practical advisor” is easier to apply.
For a comparison, define the decision criteria before asking for a recommendation.
A reviewer can check whether every requested part is present instead of reading a long answer and guessing what it was meant to accomplish.
Do not ask for an arbitrary number of sections just to make a document look substantial.
or brand claim that would be unsafe in the final answer.
The tool may treat the example as evidence even when you intended it only as a style reference.
Combining “write this and make sure it is accurate” encourages the tool to approve its own work without showing what it checked.
Before using an answer, run a verification pass with explicit checks.
Ask whether the title matches the body and whether the call to action matches the actual business offer.
For marketing content, check that the offer, audience, and destination are consistent.
A concise prompt with a clear outcome and trusted source material will usually outperform a long prompt filled with generic advice.
Use this template as a starting point: “Task: describe the result.
If a required fact is missing, mark it NEEDS REVIEW instead of guessing.

The tool can help with speed and organization.
The business remains responsible for the facts, promises, and decisions that reach customers.
